title: Brute-force SSH against authentication server
description: Attacker from 203.0.113.10 attempted 25 password guesses against user 'admin' on srv-auth-01 within 30 seconds, eventually succeeding on attempt 26.
attack_pattern: Repeated SSH AUTH_FAILURE from single source IP to single destination, same username, short time window
log_characteristics: AUTH_FAILURE events with source_ip=203.0.113.10, destination_ip=10.0.0.5, username=admin, protocol=ssh, status=REJECTED; one final AUTH_SUCCESS
analyst_investigation: Source IP mapped to simulated attacker range. No prior successful login from this IP. Single target account suggests targeted guessing rather than spray.

steps: Block source IP at perimeter firewall
Review auth logs for lateral movement
response_playbook.lessons_learned: Single-account brute force succeeds when MFA absent

resolution: IP blocked, password reset, MFA mandated for privileged accounts
lessons_learned: Password-only auth on privileged accounts is a critical gap; MFA should be mandatory.

title: PowerShell encoded command execution on user workstation
description: User jdoe on ws-user-07 executed powershell.exe -enc <base64> containing a base64-encoded script that enumerated local groups and attempted credential dumping.
attack_pattern: PowerShell process with -enc/-encodedcommand flag, executed by standard user, command contains encoded payload
log_characteristics: POWERSHELL_EXEC event with command containing -enc and long base64 string; source_ip=10.0.0.60, username=jdoe
analyst_investigation: Base64 payload decoded offline; contained Get-LocalGroupMember and sekurlsa::logonpasswords attempts. User account not compromised prior — likely phishing delivery.

steps: Block PowerShell -enc via AppLocker if feasible
response_playbook.lessons_learned: Encoded PowerShell is a strong indicator of malicious execution; AppLocker can mitigate

resolution: Host reimaged, user creds reset, AppLocker rule deployed
lessons_learned: User education on phishing + execution policy hardening reduces recurrence.

title: C2 beacon to known malicious IP
description: Workstation ws-user-07 established TLS connection to 198.51.100.9 (known malware download server) on port 443, repeating every 60 seconds.
attack_pattern: Repeated NETWORK_CONNECTION to IP on simulated malicious list, consistent interval, standard HTTPS port
log_characteristics: NETWORK_CONNECTION events with destination_ip=198.51.100.9, destination_port=443, protocol=tcp, status=ESTABLISHED, regular 60s interval
analyst_investigation: Destination IP on threat intel feed for malware distribution. No data exfil observed in logs (simulated). Host process unknown — likely scheduled task or service.

response_playbook.lessons_learned: Regular beaconing intervals suggest automated implant; scheduled task persistence common

resolution: IP blocked, host reimaged, persistence removed
lessons_learned: Egress filtering to known-malicious IPs catches C2 early; host-based detection needed for process identification.

title: Suspicious command enumeration via whoami / net user
description: User jdoe on ws-user-07 ran whoami, net user administrator, and wmic process list full within 10 seconds — classic post-exploitation enumeration.
attack_pattern: Rapid sequence of reconnaissance commands (whoami, net user, wmic) from same user/session
log_characteristics: COMMAND_EXEC events with commands matching suspicious patterns: whoami, net user administrator, wmic process list full; source_ip=10.0.0.60, username=jdoe
analyst_investigation: Commands executed interactively (not scripted). User claims legitimate admin task but sequence matches post-exploit enumeration. No prior alerts on this host.

steps: If unauthorized: reset credentials, isolate host
Check for scheduled tasks / services created
response_playbook.lessons_learned: Interactive enumeration often precedes privilege escalation; context (user role, time) is critical

resolution: User confirmed authorized admin activity; alert closed as benign after verification
lessons_learned: Legitimate admin activity can mimic attack patterns — always verify context before response.

title: Password spray against multiple accounts
description: Attacker from 198.51.100.5 attempted one login each against 20 different usernames on srv-auth-01 within 2 minutes — low-and-slow spray.
attack_pattern: AUTH_FAILURE from single source IP against many distinct usernames, same target, low rate
log_characteristics: AUTH_FAILURE events with source_ip=198.51.100.5, destination_ip=10.0.0.5, 20 distinct usernames, protocol=ssh, 5-10s intervals
analyst_investigation: Source IP on malicious list. Single attempt per account evades single-account threshold. No successes observed.

steps: Monitor for successful auth from this IP
Review all accounts for unauthorized access
response_playbook.lessons_learned: Spray attacks bypass per-account thresholds; IP reputation + rate limiting essential

resolution: IP blocked, account lockout threshold lowered to 3 failures/5min
lessons_learned: Detection must correlate across usernames, not just per-account counts.
